asA: chain author on a downstream product (a Worker-style web app or a library), and the verifier recording the result
iWant: to declare my app entry and harness once and have the result recorded beside the TEST verdict
soThat: Finalise reads test strength for the reviewed head without running anything
title: A chain author on a downstream product declares its entry and harness and the verifier records the result for Finalise

acceptanceCriteria.description: [happy] Given a fixture branch whose HEAD is a REVIEW: commit adding a MERGE/PASS review.json for H touching AC-101-1, and a passing test-strength run, when rcf audit test-strength --record runs, then it exits 0 and writes rcf/verdicts/<H12>/test-strength.json parsing as TestStrengthReport v1 with head the full sha of H, scope "reviewVerdict" and criteria [AC-101-1]; a FAIL run with --record writes the report too (result fail) and exits 4.

[failure] Given an uncommitted change to src/x.js, rcf audit test-strength --record exits 4 with stderr "test-strength: refused: working tree is dirty; a record names a committed head"; given a "BUILD:" commit after H that changed src/x.js, it exits 4 with "test-strength: refused: HEAD differs from the reviewed head <H7> outside rcf/verdicts/, rcf/verify-reports/ and FINALISE classes"; given no REVIEW verdict reachable from HEAD, with or without --acs or --fbs, it exits 2 with "test-strength: --record needs a REVIEW verdict reachable from HEAD"; none writes a file, and a FINALISE: commit inside FINALISE classes after H does not refuse.

[happy] Given a fixture Worker-style app whose rcf/test-strength.json declares entry [{"kind": "worker", "path": "src/index.js"}], harness ["test/harness/**"] and edge ["undici"], and a bound test that imports test/harness/worker.js (which imports src/index.js and calls its fetch with an outbound stand-in), when rcf audit test-strength --acs AC-101-1 runs, then the structural check passes; a bound test importing src/routes/pay.js directly fails with "imports src/routes/pay.js (not the app entry or the harness)".

[edge] Given a fixture library whose rcf/test-strength.json declares entry [{"kind": "module", "path": "src/index.js"}] and whose bound test imports the package by its own name (resolved through its exports map to src/index.js), the structural check passes; the same test importing ../src/index.js by relative path also passes (it is the entry), and importing ../src/internal.js fails with the imports finding.

[must-not] rcf audit test-strength never deploys, never opens a network connection of its own and never writes outside rcf/verdicts/<H12>/ in the project, with or without --record: not in its working tree, not under its node_modules or an ancestor's up to the repository root, and not in its .git, whatever the runner kind, the runner's own configuration (a vitest or playwright config, a globalSetup) or a `runners` entry's `argv` (a trailing `--`, a shell launcher) leads a bound test run to write there by creating a path; "its node_modules" means the real location of the project's node_modules, following symbolic links, and the real location of each ancestor's node_modules; every bound test runs in a working copy of HEAD the audit makes in its own scratch directory, whose node_modules directory is the audit's own, its entries linking the project's installed packages; a scratch directory that cannot be removed is named in one stderr line "[warn] test-strength: scratch directory <dir> could not be removed"; on an error exit the audit still runs the backstop and the warn line, and the message names the scratch path; on every exit, including a not-run or cannot-run exit, the audit runs the backstop, and a path it finds is named whatever else the run was about to report; a malformed rcf/test-strength.json (unparsable, an entry kind outside bin, module and worker, or an empty harness list) exits 2 naming the field and runs no test.

[failure] Given a bound test that writes a file at an absolute path inside the project outside rcf/verdicts/<H12>/, when `rcf audit test-strength` runs, then it compares the project tree (node_modules and every dot directory included, .git excluded) before and after the bound test runs, exits 2 with a stderr line "test-strength: a bound test run wrote <path> in the project" naming the first such path, and records nothing even with --record.

[failure] On SIGINT or SIGTERM during a run, `rcf audit test-strength` kills the process group of every bound test run it started, removes its scratch directory (its working copies within it), leaves no entry in the project's .git, and exits 130 for SIGINT or 143 for SIGTERM.

[happy] Given a fixture pnpm workspace whose rcf project is its root and a criterion bound to a node:test test in `apps/api/test/` importing a package installed only in `apps/api/node_modules`, when `rcf audit test-strength --acs <id>` runs over a working copy whose node_modules links follow TAC-4155's link set, then the unmutated run is green and it exits 0 and no mutant survived (stdout the PASS line, no "the unmutated run is red" line).

[happy] Given a criterion whose Code Node is a symbol in `apps/lib`, bound to a test in `apps/api` importing `@ws/lib` by name (a workspace package link), when the audit runs, then each mutant is applied in the copy's `apps/lib` and a mutant the test catches is killed, never survived (exit 0 with the PASS line, and with --json no mutant of the symbol survived).

[happy] Given a test in `apps/api` reading `fixtures/config.json` relative to `apps/api`, when the audit runs, then it runs at its package directory with `<file>` relative to it and the unmutated run is green (exit 0 with the PASS line); a test with no package.json between it and the rcf project root runs at the rcf project root. The package directory is the default for every runner kind `rcf/test-strength.json` allows: a nodeTest, vitest or playwright `runners` entry and the legacy `runner` alike, so a bound test under each kind reading `fixtures/config.json` relative to its package runs green. A package is the nearest directory at HEAD from the test file up to the rcf project root holding a package.json, else the rcf project root.

[must-not] Given an rcf project in `packages/a` and a sibling `packages/b` with its own node_modules, when a bound test writes under `packages/b/node_modules` through the copy's links, then the audit exits 2 with "test-strength: a bound test run wrote <path> in the project", `<path>` relative to the rcf project root (`../b/node_modules/bpkg/w.txt` for a write to `packages/b/node_modules/bpkg/w.txt`).

[must-not] Given the help paragraph of `rcf audit test-strength` rewritten for workspace working copies, when `rcf audit test-strength --help` runs, then it exits 0 and its output, whitespace collapsed, still holds the backstop sentence "Nothing in the project is written outside rcf/verdicts/<H12>/: the audit compares the project tree (node_modules and every dot directory included, .git excluded) and every node_modules directory on Node's module resolution path above it, up to the repository root, before and after the bound tests run, and a path a bound test run wrote there exits 2 "test-strength: a bound test run wrote <path> in the project" (a path above the project named relative to it) and records nothing."

[failure] Given a workspace package whose bound test needs its node_modules linked in the working copy (TAC-4155 responsibilities[4]), when either git ls-tree with which `rcf audit test-strength` reads HEAD fails, the listing of every package.json directory at HEAD or the listing of the files at HEAD (`git ls-tree -r --name-only HEAD`), then the audit exits 2 with a stderr line naming the command that failed, "test-strength: cannot list the workspace packages at <h7>: git ls-tree failed: <git's stderr, trimmed>" for the first and "test-strength: cannot list the files at <h7>: git ls-tree -r --name-only HEAD failed: <git's stderr, trimmed>" for the second, runs no bound test (no "the unmutated run is red" line) and prints no verdict line, where 0.40.0 went on as if the repository held no workspace package, or no file at HEAD.

[failure] Given a bound test reaching a workspace package by name through a symbolic-link entry that the working copy would re-point to the package inside the copy (TAC-4155 responsibilities[4]), and that package's entry not committed at HEAD (such as gitignored build output in `dist/`), the entry being, in this order, `exports` (a string is the entry; a conditional map is resolved for the `"."` subpath by Node's rule, the first matching key in the map's own order among the active conditions for an import from Node (`node`, `import`, `module-sync`, `default`), a nested map walked the same way; a map with no `"."` subpath and no matching condition means no entry, which counts as not committed), else `main`, else `index.js` (looked for in the package directory in the project's working tree, not at HEAD), when `rcf audit test-strength` runs, then the working copy keeps that link at the repo's own package (the built one, as 0.39.0 links it: an absolute link to the project's own entry) and the run proceeds, and stderr carries the notice line "test-strength: <link> stays at the repo's own <package>: its entry <entry> is build output not committed at <h7>; mutants in <package> are not the code this test imports", or, where the package has no entry, its second form "test-strength: <link> stays at the repo's own <package>: its package.json names no entry committed at <h7> (exports names no entry for ".") when the package.json has an exports field, else (no main, no index.js); mutants in <package> are not the code this test imports", once per link per run, however many working copies the run makes, `<link>` the symbolic-link entry and `<package>` the package directory, each relative to the rcf project root (`node_modules/@ws/lib` and `apps/lib` in a hoisted npm workspace), and `<entry>` relative to the package directory (`dist/index.js`); on a run that proceeds past a green unmutated run, the notice lines follow AC-19904-12's line when that line prints and lead stderr otherwise; on a red unmutated run from another cause (such as a test reading a path relative to the rcf project root), the unmutated-run line and the "cwd": "project" hint stay as AC-19902-9 and AC-19904-11 state them and the notice line follows the hint; the notice is no exit 2: the exit code and the verdict line are the run's own (exit 0 and the PASS line when every mutant is killed; exit 4 and the FAIL line when a mutant in `<package>`, which the test does not import, survives), where 0.40.0 re-pointed the link into a copy without the entry and the unmutated run was red (exit 2).

[happy] Given the backstop paragraph of `rcf audit test-strength --help`, which the 0.40.0 Known issue says describes the bound-test backstop more narrowly than the audit applies it, when `rcf audit test-strength --help` runs, then it exits 0 and its output, whitespace collapsed, holds, beside the backstop sentence AC-19903-12 pins, the sentence "Each node_modules directory it compares is read at its real path (where node_modules is a symbolic link, the directory it points to), and it compares the repository's .git as well, a write there named relative to the project (.git/<path> at the repository root, ../.git/<path> one directory below it)."
